channel.title: Mountain State Spotlight - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Mountain State Spotlight (mountainstatespotlight.org)

item.title: West Virginians are still dying from drug overdoses as lawmakers continue to restrict effective programs
item.description: State lawmakers have tightly constrained how people with substance use disorder can get clean syringes, medication and treatment.

item.title: Despite concerns about power bills and property rights, lawmakers race to prop up the coal industry
item.description: Between tax cuts and reducing regulations for the coal industry, several pieces of legislation are moving quickly between the House and the Senate.

item.title: As public schools across West Virginia face financial crisis, lawmakers watered down help
item.description: Going into the session, West Virginia’s failing public schools struggled to stay afloat. Legislators haven’t done much to help.

item.title: Days left for lawmakers to protect West Virginia's internet customers
item.description: Federal broadband funding is coming, but WV lawmakers did little this session to help people struggling with their internet now.

item.title: What West Virginia lawmakers did — and didn’t do — during the 2026 legislative session
item.description: As the 2026 session came to a close, many of the state’s biggest challenges, from rising power bills to public schools, saw little progress.

item.title: Five takeaways from West Virginia’s 2026-2027 state budget
item.description: Tax cuts, education funding, clean water, flooding and more: Here’s what lawmakers’ budget says about their priorities

item.title: Lawmakers fill some foster care gaps after Mountain State Spotlight investigation revealed the state is failing kids - Mountain State Spotlight
item.description: After Mountain State Spotlight reporting, West Virginia lawmakers passed bills expanding support for foster youth and kinship caregivers.

item.title: Politicians are making it harder to see who’s buying influence in West Virginia
item.description: A new law redacts a donor’s employer from campaign finance statements, making it harder to determine who is funding a politician.

item.title: Meet the people behind the Democrats’ surge in candidates for the 2026 election
item.description: Coming from different walks of life, here’s the story behind why five people have decided to run on the Democratic ticket this year.

item.title: A major barrier to jobs for West Virginians persists as lawmakers fail to address public transit needs
item.description: West Virginians need buses to get to work, medical appointments and grocery stores. Lawmakers advanced no new transit funding, even as routes get cut.
